Definition: from G1537 and εἶμι (to go); to issue, i.e. leave (a place), escape (to the shore):--depart, get (to land), go out.
BiblicalUsage: éxeimi is the word for depart, get (to land), go out. In Acts 13:42, the text says "And when the Jews were gone out of the synagogue." In Acts 17:15, the text says "they departed."
TheologicalSignificance: I believe éxeimi shows us that the gospel was never meant to stay where it started — it goes out, because God sends it out. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
RelatedEvents: Paul's Missionary Journeys; Paul Preaches at Pisidian Antioch; Paul at Berea
